test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following locations is correct for installing the oil filter in the engine?

options.text: Downstream of coolers in order to filter if any solid part from coolers enters the oil lines
In between coolers and the oil lines coming from sump
After lines going to supply the oil to the bearing after coolers
Up stream of coolers in order to filter if any solid part from coolers lives the oil lines

solution:
The correct answer is __Downstream of coolers in order to filter if any solid part from coolers enters the oil lines.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Oil filters__ are essential for removing contaminants from the oil.
 
• Placing the filter downstream of coolers ensures that any solid particles from the cooler are captured before entering sensitive engine components.
 
• This placement protects critical parts like bearings and pistons from damage due to debris.
 
• It ensures smoother operation of the engine and extends the lifespan of components.
 
• Regular maintenance and replacement of the oil filter are crucial for engine health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Oil Cooler:**

 
 
• The oil cooler is a device used to regulate the temperature of the engine oil.
 
• It prevents overheating and ensures optimal lubrication of engine components.
 
 
 
• **Oil Lines: **
 
 
• Oil lines transport the oil to various engine parts for lubrication and cooling.
 
• Proper filtration is vital to avoid clogging or damage to these lines.
 
 
 
• **Bearings:**
 
 
• Engine bearings rely on clean oil to reduce friction and prevent wear.
 
• Contaminated oil can lead to bearing failure and engine damage.
